### Admissions
- **Score:** 0.78977093075325
- **URL:** /standard-page/admissions
- **Description:** This page covers the shape of admission at Northmoor. The detail for your situation is on the linked pages, and the admissions office answers questions directly.
Undergraduate admission
We admit for fall entry in all seven undergraduate programs, and for spring entry in Environmental Science and Marine Policy.
Applications are reviewed as a whole. High school coursework and grades matter most, and the specific requirements differ by program — Oceanography and Marine Engineering require calculus and mean it, while Marine Biology recommends physics and does not require it. Each program page states its own requirements.
We read personal statements carefully. A statement describing why this subject and why a specialized institution is more useful to us than a general account of academic achievement.
Applicants who fall short on one requirement are sometimes admitted with a first-semester condition attached rather than declined. If your record is unusual, apply and explain it.
Graduate admission
The five graduate programs work differently from one another, and the difference matters.
The doctoral program admits by supervisor. Find the person whose work you want to do and write to them before you apply. Applications arriving without that conversation are at a real disadvantage, because the decision is made by the prospective supervisor and turns on research fit and funding.
The research master's programs — Marine Mammal Science and Ocean Engineering — expect a specific undergraduate background and are explicit about what it is. Contact with a prospective supervisor helps here too.
The professional master's programs — Coastal Resilience and Marine Resource Management — are deliberately open on discipline and weight professional experience heavily.
Graduate applications close in January for fall entry.
A note on graduate-level specializations
Several subjects people write to us about are graduate programs rather than undergraduate ones. Marine mammal science is the most common. If that is what you want to do, the route is an undergraduate degree in marine biology first — here or elsewhere — and then a graduate application. That is the normal path, not a consolation.
What it costs
Tuition, fees and financial aid are set out in full on the tuition and financial aid page. Costs are published there and nowhere else on this site, so that there is one figure rather than several that drift.
Financial aid questions go to the aid team through the admissions office. Please ask early; the aid timeline runs ahead of the admission timeline.
Deadlines
Undergraduate applications for fall entry close on 15 January. Spring entry closes on 1 October. Graduate applications close on 15 January for fall entry.
Talking to us
Rosa Delgado's office handles all admission inquiries, undergraduate and graduate. Visiting is strongly encouraged — see the visit page for open days and campus tours.

### How to Apply
- **Score:** 0.77846486266884
- **URL:** /standard-page/how-to-apply
- **Description:** This page is the procedure. The admissions page covers what we look for and how the different programs differ.
Undergraduate
1. Choose your program. You apply to a specific degree, not to the university generally. Program requirements differ — check the page for the one you want before you start.
2. Submit the application. Through the common application or directly through our own form, whichever you prefer. There is no advantage to either.
3. Send transcripts. Official high school transcripts, and college transcripts if you have taken any coursework. Transfer applicants should send everything.
4. Write the personal statement. One to two pages. Tell us why this subject and why a specialized institution. We read these properly.
5. One letter of recommendation. From a teacher in a relevant subject where possible. One good letter is better than three general ones.
6. File for financial aid separately, and early. The aid deadline is 1 February and runs ahead of the admission timeline. Do not wait for an admission decision.
Standardized test scores are optional and considered where submitted.
Deadlines. 15 January for fall entry. 1 October for spring entry, available in Environmental Science and Marine Policy only.
Graduate
1. Contact a prospective supervisor first if you are applying to the doctoral program or to either research master's. This is not a formality — for the doctorate, the admission decision is made by the supervisor.
2. Submit the application with transcripts, a research or professional statement, and a curriculum vitae.
3. Three letters of recommendation. Academic references for research programs; professional references are appropriate for the professional master's programs.
4. English language testing if your degree was not taught in English.
Deadline. 15 January for fall entry, all graduate programs.
Transfer applicants
We accept transfer students into all undergraduate programs. Credit is evaluated course by course after admission, and laboratory and field courses transfer less predictably than lecture courses — ask before assuming.
International applicants
Applications follow the same process with the addition of English language testing and, after admission, visa documentation. The admissions office handles the second and can talk you through the timeline, which is longer than most applicants expect.
After you apply
Undergraduate decisions go out from mid-March. Graduate decisions vary by program and supervisor availability, usually between February and April.
Questions at any stage go to the admissions office.

### Rosa Delgado
- **Score:** 0.77170222874541
- **URL:** /person/rosa-delgado
- **Description:** Rosa Delgado has run admissions at Northmoor since 2018. She and her team handle applications for all twelve programs, coordinate the open days, and manage the campus visit program.
She is the first point of contact for questions about entry requirements, application deadlines and transfer credit. Questions about financial aid go to her office as well, though the aid team handles the detail.
Her standing advice to prospective students is to visit if there is any way to manage it, and to come in bad weather if possible. A campus on the coast looks appealing in September. What a student needs to know is whether they still want to be here in February.

### Admisiones
- **Score:** 0.7703018982481
- **URL:** /es/node/5
- **Description:** Esta página describe el panorama general de la admisión en Northmoor. Los detalles para su situación particular están en las páginas enlazadas, y la oficina de admisiones responde preguntas directamente.
Admisión de licenciatura
La universidad admite ingreso de otoño en las siete licenciaturas, e ingreso de primavera en Ciencias Ambientales (Environmental Science) y Política Marina (Marine Policy).
Las solicitudes se evalúan de manera integral. Lo que más importa son las materias cursadas y las calificaciones de la educación secundaria, y los requisitos específicos varían según el programa: Oceanografía e Ingeniería Marina exigen cálculo y lo exigen en serio, mientras que Biología Marina recomienda física sin exigirla. Cada página de programa indica sus propios requisitos.
Las cartas de motivación se leen con atención. Una carta que explique por qué esta disciplina y por qué una institución especializada resulta más útil que un relato general de logros académicos.
Los postulantes que no cumplen un requisito a veces son admitidos con una condición para el primer semestre en lugar de ser rechazados. Si su historial académico es poco común, postule y explíquelo.
Admisión de posgrado
Los cinco programas de posgrado funcionan de manera distinta entre sí, y la diferencia importa.
El programa doctoral admite por asesor. Identifique a la persona cuyo trabajo desea realizar y escríbale antes de postular. Las solicitudes que llegan sin esa conversación previa están en real desventaja, porque la decisión la toma el posible asesor y depende de la afinidad de investigación y del financiamiento disponible.
Las maestrías de investigación — Ciencia de Mamíferos Marinos (Marine Mammal Science) e Ingeniería Oceánica (Ocean Engineering) — requieren una formación de licenciatura específica y son explícitas al respecto. El contacto con un posible asesor también ayuda en este caso.
Las maestrías profesionales — Resiliencia Costera (Coastal Resilience) y Gestión de Recursos Marinos (Marine Resource Management) — son deliberadamente abiertas en cuanto a la disciplina de origen y otorgan un peso considerable a la experiencia profesional.
Las solicitudes de posgrado cierran en enero para el ingreso de otoño.
Una nota sobre especializaciones de posgrado
Varios de los temas sobre los que se nos escribe corresponden a programas de posgrado y no de licenciatura. La ciencia de mamíferos marinos es el más frecuente. Si eso es lo que desea estudiar, la vía es cursar primero una licenciatura en biología marina —aquí o en otra institución— y luego postular a un posgrado. Ese es el camino normal, no un premio de consuelo.
Cuánto cuesta
La matrícula, las cuotas y la ayuda financiera se detallan por completo en la página de matrícula y ayuda financiera. Los costos se publican únicamente allí y en ningún otro lugar de este sitio, para que exista una sola cifra en lugar de varias que se desactualicen entre sí.
Las preguntas sobre ayuda financiera se dirigen al equipo de ayuda financiera a través de la oficina de admisiones. Por favor, consulte con anticipación: el cronograma de ayuda financiera se adelanta al cronograma de admisión.
Fechas límite
Las solicitudes de licenciatura para el ingreso de otoño cierran el 15 de enero. El ingreso de primavera cierra el 1 de octubre. Las solicitudes de posgrado cierran el 15 de enero para el ingreso de otoño.
Cómo comunicarse con nosotros
La oficina de Rosa Delgado atiende todas las consultas de admisión, tanto de licenciatura como de posgrado. Se recomienda encarecidamente visitar el campus: consulte la página de visitas para conocer las jornadas de puertas abiertas y los recorridos por el campus.

description.label: Description
values:
This page covers the shape of admission at Northmoor. The detail for your situation is on the linked pages, and the admissions office answers questions directly.
Undergraduate admission
We admit for fall entry in all seven undergraduate programs, and for spring entry in Environmental Science and Marine Policy.
Applications are reviewed as a whole. High school coursework and grades matter most, and the specific requirements differ by program — Oceanography and Marine Engineering require calculus and mean it, while Marine Biology recommends physics and does not require it. Each program page states its own requirements.
We read personal statements carefully. A statement describing why this subject and why a specialized institution is more useful to us than a general account of academic achievement.
Applicants who fall short on one requirement are sometimes admitted with a first-semester condition attached rather than declined. If your record is unusual, apply and explain it.
Graduate admission
The five graduate programs work differently from one another, and the difference matters.
The doctoral program admits by supervisor. Find the person whose work you want to do and write to them before you apply. Applications arriving without that conversation are at a real disadvantage, because the decision is made by the prospective supervisor and turns on research fit and funding.
The research master's programs — Marine Mammal Science and Ocean Engineering — expect a specific undergraduate background and are explicit about what it is. Contact with a prospective supervisor helps here too.
The professional master's programs — Coastal Resilience and Marine Resource Management — are deliberately open on discipline and weight professional experience heavily.
Graduate applications close in January for fall entry.
A note on graduate-level specializations
Several subjects people write to us about are graduate programs rather than undergraduate ones. Marine mammal science is the most common. If that is what you want to do, the route is an undergraduate degree in marine biology first — here or elsewhere — and then a graduate application. That is the normal path, not a consolation.
What it costs
Tuition, fees and financial aid are set out in full on the tuition and financial aid page. Costs are published there and nowhere else on this site, so that there is one figure rather than several that drift.
Financial aid questions go to the aid team through the admissions office. Please ask early; the aid timeline runs ahead of the admission timeline.
Deadlines
Undergraduate applications for fall entry close on 15 January. Spring entry closes on 1 October. Graduate applications close on 15 January for fall entry.
Talking to us
Rosa Delgado's office handles all admission inquiries, undergraduate and graduate. Visiting is strongly encouraged — see the visit page for open days and campus tours.

description.label: Description
values:
This page is the procedure. The admissions page covers what we look for and how the different programs differ.
Undergraduate
1. Choose your program. You apply to a specific degree, not to the university generally. Program requirements differ — check the page for the one you want before you start.
2. Submit the application. Through the common application or directly through our own form, whichever you prefer. There is no advantage to either.
3. Send transcripts. Official high school transcripts, and college transcripts if you have taken any coursework. Transfer applicants should send everything.
4. Write the personal statement. One to two pages. Tell us why this subject and why a specialized institution. We read these properly.
5. One letter of recommendation. From a teacher in a relevant subject where possible. One good letter is better than three general ones.
6. File for financial aid separately, and early. The aid deadline is 1 February and runs ahead of the admission timeline. Do not wait for an admission decision.
Standardized test scores are optional and considered where submitted.
Deadlines. 15 January for fall entry. 1 October for spring entry, available in Environmental Science and Marine Policy only.
Graduate
1. Contact a prospective supervisor first if you are applying to the doctoral program or to either research master's. This is not a formality — for the doctorate, the admission decision is made by the supervisor.
2. Submit the application with transcripts, a research or professional statement, and a curriculum vitae.
3. Three letters of recommendation. Academic references for research programs; professional references are appropriate for the professional master's programs.
4. English language testing if your degree was not taught in English.
Deadline. 15 January for fall entry, all graduate programs.
Transfer applicants
We accept transfer students into all undergraduate programs. Credit is evaluated course by course after admission, and laboratory and field courses transfer less predictably than lecture courses — ask before assuming.
International applicants
Applications follow the same process with the addition of English language testing and, after admission, visa documentation. The admissions office handles the second and can talk you through the timeline, which is longer than most applicants expect.
After you apply
Undergraduate decisions go out from mid-March. Graduate decisions vary by program and supervisor availability, usually between February and April.
Questions at any stage go to the admissions office.

- **Score:** 0.77846486266884
- **URL:** /standard-page/how-to-apply
- **Description:** This page is the procedure. The admissions page covers what we look for and how the different programs differ.
Undergraduate
1. Choose your program. You apply to a specific degree, not to the university generally. Program requirements differ — check the page for the one you want before you start.
2. Submit the application. Through the common application or directly through our own form, whichever you prefer. There is no advantage to either.
3. Send transcripts. Official high school transcripts, and college transcripts if you have taken any coursework. Transfer applicants should send everything.
4. Write the personal statement. One to two pages. Tell us why this subject and why a specialized institution. We read these properly.
5. One letter of recommendation. From a teacher in a relevant subject where possible. One good letter is better than three general ones.
6. File for financial aid separately, and early. The aid deadline is 1 February and runs ahead of the admission timeline. Do not wait for an admission decision.
Standardized test scores are optional and considered where submitted.
Deadlines. 15 January for fall entry. 1 October for spring entry, available in Environmental Science and Marine Policy only.
Graduate
1. Contact a prospective supervisor first if you are applying to the doctoral program or to either research master's. This is not a formality — for the doctorate, the admission decision is made by the supervisor.
2. Submit the application with transcripts, a research or professional statement, and a curriculum vitae.
3. Three letters of recommendation. Academic references for research programs; professional references are appropriate for the professional master's programs.
4. English language testing if your degree was not taught in English.
Deadline. 15 January for fall entry, all graduate programs.
Transfer applicants
We accept transfer students into all undergraduate programs. Credit is evaluated course by course after admission, and laboratory and field courses transfer less predictably than lecture courses — ask before assuming.
International applicants
Applications follow the same process with the addition of English language testing and, after admission, visa documentation. The admissions office handles the second and can talk you through the timeline, which is longer than most applicants expect.
After you apply
Undergraduate decisions go out from mid-March. Graduate decisions vary by program and supervisor availability, usually between February and April.
Questions at any stage go to the admissions office.

### Rosa Delgado
- **Score:** 0.77170222874541
- **URL:** /person/rosa-delgado
- **Description:** Rosa Delgado has run admissions at Northmoor since 2018. She and her team handle applications for all twelve programs, coordinate the open days, and manage the campus visit program.
She is the first point of contact for questions about entry requirements, application deadlines and transfer credit. Questions about financial aid go to her office as well, though the aid team handles the detail.
Her standing advice to prospective students is to visit if there is any way to manage it, and to come in bad weather if possible. A campus on the coast looks appealing in September. What a student needs to know is whether they still want to be here in February.

### Admisiones
- **Score:** 0.7703018982481
- **URL:** /es/node/5
- **Description:** Esta página describe el panorama general de la admisión en Northmoor. Los detalles para su situación particular están en las páginas enlazadas, y la oficina de admisiones responde preguntas directamente.
Admisión de licenciatura
La universidad admite ingreso de otoño en las siete licenciaturas, e ingreso de primavera en Ciencias Ambientales (Environmental Science) y Política Marina (Marine Policy).
Las solicitudes se evalúan de manera integral. Lo que más importa son las materias cursadas y las calificaciones de la educación secundaria, y los requisitos específicos varían según el programa: Oceanografía e Ingeniería Marina exigen cálculo y lo exigen en serio, mientras que Biología Marina recomienda física sin exigirla. Cada página de programa indica sus propios requisitos.
Las cartas de motivación se leen con atención. Una carta que explique por qué esta disciplina y por qué una institución especializada resulta más útil que un relato general de logros académicos.
Los postulantes que no cumplen un requisito a veces son admitidos con una condición para el primer semestre en lugar de ser rechazados. Si su historial académico es poco común, postule y explíquelo.
Admisión de posgrado
Los cinco programas de posgrado funcionan de manera distinta entre sí, y la diferencia importa.
El programa doctoral admite por asesor. Identifique a la persona cuyo trabajo desea realizar y escríbale antes de postular. Las solicitudes que llegan sin esa conversación previa están en real desventaja, porque la decisión la toma el posible asesor y depende de la afinidad de investigación y del financiamiento disponible.
Las maestrías de investigación — Ciencia de Mamíferos Marinos (Marine Mammal Science) e Ingeniería Oceánica (Ocean Engineering) — requieren una formación de licenciatura específica y son explícitas al respecto. El contacto con un posible asesor también ayuda en este caso.
Las maestrías profesionales — Resiliencia Costera (Coastal Resilience) y Gestión de Recursos Marinos (Marine Resource Management) — son deliberadamente abiertas en cuanto a la disciplina de origen y otorgan un peso considerable a la experiencia profesional.
Las solicitudes de posgrado cierran en enero para el ingreso de otoño.
Una nota sobre especializaciones de posgrado
Varios de los temas sobre los que se nos escribe corresponden a programas de posgrado y no de licenciatura. La ciencia de mamíferos marinos es el más frecuente. Si eso es lo que desea estudiar, la vía es cursar primero una licenciatura en biología marina —aquí o en otra institución— y luego postular a un posgrado. Ese es el camino normal, no un premio de consuelo.
Cuánto cuesta
La matrícula, las cuotas y la ayuda financiera se detallan por completo en la página de matrícula y ayuda financiera. Los costos se publican únicamente allí y en ningún otro lugar de este sitio, para que exista una sola cifra en lugar de varias que se desactualicen entre sí.
Las preguntas sobre ayuda financiera se dirigen al equipo de ayuda financiera a través de la oficina de admisiones. Por favor, consulte con anticipación: el cronograma de ayuda financiera se adelanta al cronograma de admisión.
Fechas límite
Las solicitudes de licenciatura para el ingreso de otoño cierran el 15 de enero. El ingreso de primavera cierra el 1 de octubre. Las solicitudes de posgrado cierran el 15 de enero para el ingreso de otoño.
Cómo comunicarse con nosotros
La oficina de Rosa Delgado atiende todas las consultas de admisión, tanto de licenciatura como de posgrado. Se recomienda encarecidamente visitar el campus: consulte la página de visitas para conocer las jornadas de puertas abiertas y los recorridos por el campus.
